title: Psalm 57: My Heart Is Fixed
body:
Read the chapter → [Psalms 57](/bible/psalms/57)

[Psalm 57](/bible/psalms/57) makes the shadow of the Most High's wings a refuge until the calamities be overpast. The teaching locates that refuge in meditating on the scriptures day and night, in the secret place of the Most High, and lifts up the deliverance He sends from heaven, illustrated by the angels that scourged Heliodorus in 2 Maccabees. The heart that is fixed is the tree planted by the rivers of water that will not be swayed by doctrines, looks, or money, and no one takes its crown.

**[Psalms 57:1](/bible/psalms/57#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/psalms/57#v1)</sup> Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me: for my soul trusteth in thee: yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge, until these calamities be overpast.

- He asks for mercy, for his soul trusts in the Most High, and makes his refuge in the shadow of His wings until the calamities be overpast.
- Where should we make our refuge? It begins with meditating on the scriptures, which is why the four chapters a day has been set up.
  - **[Joshua 1:8](/bible/joshua/1#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/joshua/1#v8)</sup> This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.

    The book of the law shall not depart from thy mouth; meditate day and night to observe and do it, and thy way shall be prosperous.
  - **[Psalms 91:1-4](/bible/psalms/91#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/psalms/91#v1)</sup> He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/psalms/91#v2)</sup> I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/psalms/91#v3)</sup> Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence.
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/psalms/91#v4)</sup> He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.

    He that dwells in the secret place of the Most High abides under the shadow of the Almighty, and His truth shall be thy shield and buckler.
  - **[Malachi 3:16](/bible/malachi/3#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/malachi/3#v16)</sup> Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another: and the Lord hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the Lord, and that thought upon his name.

    They that feared the Most High spake often one to another, a safety net of communication so our conversations stay in the law.

**[Psalms 57:2-3](/bible/psalms/57#v2)**

> <sup>[2](/bible/psalms/57#v2)</sup> I will cry unto God most high; unto God that performeth all things for me.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/psalms/57#v3)</sup> He shall send from heaven, and save me from the reproach of him that would swallow me up. Selah. God shall send forth his mercy and his truth.

- He cries unto the Most High that performs all things for him, who shall send from heaven and save him from the reproach of him that would swallow him up, sending forth His mercy and truth.
- When it says He shall send from heaven and save me, look at the history of Heliodorus, who came to take all the funds out of the temple true to the nature of Edom the grape gatherer, and the Most High sent two angels to give the heathen a righteous beating.
  - **[2 Maccabees 3:23-26](/bible/2-maccabees/3#v23)**
    > <sup>[23](/bible/2-maccabees/3#v23)</sup> Nevertheless Heliodorus executed that which was decreed.
    >
    > <sup>[24](/bible/2-maccabees/3#v24)</sup> Now as he was there present himself with his guard about the treasury, the Lord of spirits, and the Prince of all power, caused a great apparition, so that all that presumed to come in with him were astonished at the power of God, and fainted, and were sore afraid.
    >
    > <sup>[25](/bible/2-maccabees/3#v25)</sup> For there appeared unto them an horse with a terrible rider upon him, and adorned with a very fair covering, and he ran fiercely, and smote at Heliodorus with his forefeet, and it seemed that he that sat upon the horse had complete harness of gold.
    >
    > <sup>[26](/bible/2-maccabees/3#v26)</sup> Moreover two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes.

    The Most High caused a great apparition and sent a rider and two mighty young men who scourged Heliodorus continually when he came to rob the treasury.
  - **[2 Maccabees 3:34](/bible/2-maccabees/3#v34)**
    > <sup>[34](/bible/2-maccabees/3#v34)</sup> And seeing that thou hast been scourged from heaven, declare unto all men the mighty power of God. And when they had spoken these words, they appeared no more.

    Seeing thou hast been scourged from heaven, declare unto all men the mighty power of God.
  - **[Matthew 24:30-31](/bible/matthew/24#v30)**
    > <sup>[30](/bible/matthew/24#v30)</sup> And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
    >
    > <sup>[31](/bible/matthew/24#v31)</sup> And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.

    The Son of man comes in the clouds with power, and sends His angels to gather His elect, us, from the four winds because we have been scattered.

**[Psalms 57:4-6](/bible/psalms/57#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/psalms/57#v4)</sup> My soul is among lions: and I lie even among them that are set on fire, even the sons of men, whose teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/psalms/57#v5)</sup> Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; let thy glory be above all the earth.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/psalms/57#v6)</sup> They have prepared a net for my steps; my soul is bowed down: they have digged a pit before me, into the midst whereof they are fallen themselves. Selah.

- His soul is among lions and among the sons of men whose teeth are spears and arrows and their tongue a sharp sword, yet he cries that the Most High be exalted above the heavens.
- They prepared a net for his steps and digged a pit before him, but they are fallen into the midst of it themselves.

**[Psalms 57:7-11](/bible/psalms/57#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/psalms/57#v7)</sup> My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing and give praise.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/psalms/57#v8)</sup> Awake up, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp: I myself will awake early.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/psalms/57#v9)</sup> I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people: I will sing unto thee among the nations.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/psalms/57#v10)</sup> For thy mercy is great unto the heavens, and thy truth unto the clouds.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/psalms/57#v11)</sup> Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: let thy glory be above all the earth.

- David in the spirit says his heart is fixed even though all these enemies come against him; he will sing and give praise and awake early.
- A fixed heart is the tree planted by the rivers of water that will not be swayed. Doctrines will not pull you out; you will not be hasty to credit somebody by their looks or their money, and no one takes your crown.
- We praise the Most High among the nations now by wearing the fringes and beautiful garments, pushing the gospel in the streets to our people, waking up the dead state of our people while Bishop destroys Christianity week after week.
  - **[Psalms 1:1-3](/bible/psalms/1#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/psalms/1#v1)</sup> Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/psalms/1#v2)</sup> But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/psalms/1#v3)</sup> And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

    The blessed man delights in the law and meditates day and night, and is like a tree planted by the rivers of water whose leaf shall not wither.
  - **[Lamentations 3:22-23](/bible/lamentations/3#v22)**
    > <sup>[22](/bible/lamentations/3#v22)</sup> It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.
    >
    > <sup>[23](/bible/lamentations/3#v23)</sup> They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.

    It is of the Most High's mercies that we are not consumed, His compassions fail not and are new every morning.
